rule.action: Use the explicit country-year roster, harmonize country IDs, pool repeated cross-sections; do not treat respondents as a longitudinal panel.

sample_steps.rule: Resolve source missing codes before numerical comparisons; retain GEMAGE > 18 and GEMAGE < 55 under the literal age wording. Inclusion of exactly age 18 is unclear and a separate specification axis.

Main branch: closest operational reading is employed respondents, GEMWORK in {1,2} (GEMWORK3=10 as cross-check), because footnote contrasts this sample with inclusion of not-employed people. Prose instead says in the labor force; treatment of unemployed job seekers cannot be identified from GEMWORK alone. This is an uncertain origin, not a documented code. A3_M2 bypasses this step and codes not_employed.

Construct nascent and current-owner indicators and total entrepreneurial activity as defined below. MAIN quotation supports current owner-manager eligibility, while a stricter harmonized established-owner duration cutoff is not stated. Preserve the distinction as unclear.

Join independently sourced institutional/control variables by country and survey year, with mother-leave policy changes lagged one year. Childcare missing-year imputation is required but its algorithm is unspecified. Do not derive any country-year input, scale constant or missing value from published tables.

Resolve required variable availability for each model. Complete-case processing is an explicit provisional fallback, not an article-reported rule; common versus model-specific sample retention is unclear. France 2003 lacks work and education responses in the supplied harmonized source despite its inclusion in the roster. Status lacks early-year responses. Do not remove years or impute silently.

For M4–M8 retain current established business owners from step 4, not nascent-only respondents. Use the owner module for motives and firm characteristics; M7 restricts to 2002–2008 and M8 to 2005–2008. Poland contributes no eligible survey years to M8. Model-specific outcome missingness remains unclear.

For A3_M3 require the perception/network covariates. Recognize the questionnaire’s entrepreneur-dependent screening pattern from 2003 onward; no correction is described. A3_M1 uses the nascent outcome with the main sampling branch.

variables.name: postsecondary
variables.definition: Postsecondary degree or higher.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Closest mapping: 1316 or 1720 -> 1; 0,111,1212 -> 0. Harmonized postsecondary category need not distinguish completed degree from some training.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: 9999/system missing -> missing; no imputation described.

variables.name: nascent
variables.definition: Active start-up attempt with no more than three months of payments.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Provisional harmonized indicator SUBOANWT in {1,100} -> 1, 0 -> 0; source checks active effort, expected ownership and payment duration. Text quotation also permits BSTART-based screening; exact activity/ownership checks and harmonizer reclassification are unclear.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: BSTART=8,9; SUACTS=3,4,8,9; SUOWN=4,5,7,8,9,999999; SUWAGE=3,4,8,9 are missing/unknown, not zero. Harmonized transformations can embed year-specific missing handling.

variables.name: current_owner
variables.definition: Owner of a business the respondent helps manage; used for owner-subsample selection.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Closest textual reading OWNMGE=1; OMOWN in {1,2} may corroborate ownership but an extra consistency filter is not stated. OMESTBBT imposes a more-than-42-month payments condition not stated by the article. Retain as an uncertain eligibility alternative, not an automatic substitution.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: OWNMGE=8,9; OMOWN=7,8,9,999999 are nonresponse; OMOWN=3 means no personal share and requires explicit resolution if screen says owner.

variables.name: entrepreneurial_activity
variables.definition: Nascent entrepreneur or current owner-manager, counted once.

construction from source variables and c.rule: 1 if nascent=1 or current_owner=1; 0 if both resolved as 0; otherwise unresolved. Quoted screening rule BSTART=1 OR OWNMGE=1 is an alternative. TEA alone is not this outcome because it omits older businesses.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: Unresolved screening responses stay missing unless another component positively establishes activity; author rule unknown.

variables.name: limited_options
variables.definition: Reports no better choices for work as reason for involvement.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Closest direct mapping OMREASON=2 -> 1; substantive alternatives 1,3,4,6 -> 0. Mixed motive code 3 may alternatively count as limited options and is unclear. OMWHY=-1 is a possible harmonized check, not an automatic replacement.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: OMREASON=7,8,9,999999/system missing -> missing, not no; treatment of mixed/other motives unstated.

variables.name: log_business_size
variables.definition: Log of current employee count plus owner-labor allowance.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Natural log(OMNOWJOB + 1) is the closest conventional log reading; use valid nonnegative employee counts. Article first says full-time employees but later admits hours unknown; available item is headcount.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: 999999,9999997,9999999/system missing -> missing before transformation; negative counts invalid. No trimming rule given.
variables.transformations: Log(count + 1); log base not expressly stated. Outcome centering is not explicitly established despite general continuous-variable centering statement.

variables.name: high_growth
variables.definition: Expects more than five additional employees over the next five years.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Closest definition 1{OMYR5JOB - OMNOWJOB > 5}, else 0 for valid counts. Later results wording says hire more than five employees without additional; future total >5 is a non-equivalent alternative.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: For each count: 999999,9999997,9999999/system missing -> missing; do not classify unknown expectations as low growth.

variables.name: new_product
variables.definition: Product/service new and unfamiliar to all customers.

construction from source variables and c.rule: 1 -> 1; 2 or 3 -> 0; use 2002–2008 owner module.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: 7,8,9/system missing -> missing.

variables.name: new_technology
variables.definition: Product/service uses technology described as less than five years old.

construction from source variables and c.rule: 1 or 2 -> 1; 3 -> 0; 2005–2008. The source’s one-to-five-years category includes an unresolved exact five-year boundary. OMNEWTEC uses a different one-year threshold and is not equivalent.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: 7,8,9,99/system missing -> missing.

variables.name: sole_owner
variables.definition: Owns the whole business rather than sharing ownership.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Closest direct share mapping OMOWN=1 -> 1, 2 -> 0; OMOWNERS=1 versus >1 is a different count of owner-managers and a check/uncertain alternative.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: OMOWN=3 is not a valid all/part owner response; 7,8,9,999999 missing. OMOWNERS=999,9997,9999 missing.

variables.name: log_business_age_c
variables.definition: Log years since founders first received wages, profits or payments in kind, centered.

construction from source variables and c.rule: Decode payment year using its year-specific scheme, compute GEM_YR minus payment year, take natural log for positive ages, then grand mean center. Exact dating, open-ended earliest-year category, no-profits-yet and same-year cases unresolved; no +1 stated.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: Calendar scheme 9997,9998,9999; categorical scheme 13,14,15; system missing are unresolved/nonresponse. Code 12=before 1990 and year 1990=up to 1990 require explicit handling, not an invented exact year.
variables.transformations: Log then grand mean center; centering population unknown.

variables.coding of missing/refused/don't know: GEMWORK=9 or GEMWORK3=99/system missing -> missing.

inference.observation_unit: Adult respondent in a national survey; owner outcomes describe the respondent’s business. Multiple owners of a venture are not a separately documented cluster.
inference.sampling_unit: Individual adults within country-year national repeated cross-sectional samples; MAIN describes random sampling, while the dictionary notes country-specific survey designs and some quotas. Primary sampling units/strata are not supplied by the article.
inference.assignment_unit_for_country_variables: Observational country-year institutional environment, largely country-level variation; no randomized assignment.
inference.clusters: Country-year surveys nested within countries, with random intercepts and female slopes at both grouping levels. Cluster-sandwich unit and finite-cluster corrections are unstated.

tail_and_alpha_policy.alpha: Table legends define significance categories; numeric thresholds are retained only in sealed_targets.json under the target-free requirement. Exact p values and multiplicity policy are unstated.
tail_and_alpha_policy.testing: Coefficient-test statistic/distribution, likelihood-ratio df and boundary corrections are unstated; no joint quadratic-interaction tests are printed.

missing_data.reported: Childcare values for missing years were imputed, method unstated. Perception items have questionnaire-routing missingness. Innovation and technology have restricted year windows. Industry was omitted for extensive missingness. All other analytic missing-data rules are unstated.
missing_data.provisional_rule: Preserve unknowns; map documented special codes to missing before transformations; no published-cell imputation. Complete cases per model only as an uncertain implementation fallback, with a common-sample alternative recorded.
